Definition: Integration of farmer registries, agricultural input vouchers, land registrations, extension services data
Comments: No evidence of farmer registry or agricultural data integration with government data exchange systems in DRC, despite agriculture being a key sector for digital transformation per GSMA and government plans.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original source (Ecofin Agency article on data-centre investment talks) does not address agriculture data at all and was wrongly cited for this variable. A dedicated CCARDESA/World Bank Digital Agriculture Country Study for DRC found no sectoral digitalisation strategy for agriculture and little evidence of ICT integration into agricultural systems (farmer registries, input vouchers, land or extension data are not linked to any government data-exchange platform); the main digital-agriculture activity identified is Moloni, a private Vodacom/Kadea advisory platform run in partnership with the Ministry of Agriculture that provides SMS/USSD advisory and beneficiary monitoring but is not integrated into a cross-government exchange. Search also surfaced an unresolved claim (Joint SDG Fund "Digital Transformation: Democratic Republic of Congo" article, and a passing UNCDF 2025 annual-report reference to a "SDG-Data for Digital Agri Transformation" programme in DRC) describing an initiative to integrate 13 Ministry of Agriculture data platforms into a unified farmer database — but the specific figures in that article are identical to the confirmed Tanzania programme of the same name (launched Oct 2024, Dodoma/Kigoma/Ruvuma/Manyara), suggesting the DRC page may be a templating/content error rather than a genuine distinct DRC initiative. Given this unresolved source conflict, the code is raised from Unknown to "Not integrated" (documented absence of integration) rather than a higher code, and the row is flagged for human review to confirm whether a genuine DRC-specific agri-data integration programme exists.
revised_comments: Digitalisation of agriculture data in DRC remains at an early stage. A CCARDESA/World Bank digital agriculture country study finds no dedicated agricultural digitalisation strategy and little evidence that farmer registries, land records, input-voucher or extension-service data are integrated into any government data-exchange platform. The main visible digital agriculture initiative is Moloni, a Vodacom/Kadea advisory service run with the Ministry of Agriculture that delivers SMS/USSD/app-based advisory content and beneficiary monitoring to smallholder farmers, but this operates as a standalone private-sector platform rather than a component of a cross-government exchange.

Definition: Integration of social assistance programs, grant registries, beneficiary management systems
Comments: No documented operational social protection registry integration with a data exchange platform. The World Bank IDEA project ($400M, 2024) includes social protection components. DRC social protection systems are fragmented.

revision_notes: The cited iAfrica.com source describes DRC's broad $8.7bn digital plan (digital ID, tax portal, customs single window, civil registration) but does not mention social protection integration, so it does not actually support this variable. Fresh research found substantive, more recent evidence: the DRC government adopted a decree (Décret n°25/041 of 4 December 2025, following Council of Ministers approval in July 2025) creating the Registre Social Unique (RSU) — a unified socio-economic database consolidating targeting systems for poor and vulnerable households, centralising biographic, demographic and biometric data of social-programme beneficiaries under a steering committee, with explicit provisions for interoperability with other information systems. A related World Bank blog (May 2026) confirms the social registry, originally a World Bank/STEP project tool, has since been institutionalised by government decree following the 2023 dissolution of the FSRDC social fund. This is a genuine, government-anchored move toward integration, but as of the decree's issuance the RSU is newly established rather than operationally linked across the range of social assistance programmes and beneficiary systems, so the code is raised from Unknown to "Under development" rather than "Partially integrated."
revised_comments: The Democratic Republic of Congo has established a legal and institutional framework for integrating its social protection data. A December 2025 decree (Décret n°25/041) creates the Registre Social Unique (RSU), a unified socio-economic database intended to harmonise targeting systems for poor and vulnerable households across social assistance programmes, centralising beneficiaries' biographic, demographic and biometric data under a dedicated steering committee and technical management unit, with built-in provisions for interoperability with other information systems. The RSU formalises and institutionalises a social registry mechanism first developed under the World Bank-financed STEP safety-net project, following the 2023 dissolution of the former implementing agency (FSRDC) and a subsequent shift of responsibility to the Ministry of Social Affairs. Full operational integration across the range of social assistance and beneficiary-management systems is still being built out.
